articles.title: Vitamin B3 Shows 82% Progression-Free Rate in Deadly Brain Cancer — Will Oncology's Profit Machine Let This See the Light?
articles.summary: A small but striking trial found high-dose niacin kept 82% of glioblastoma patients progression-free at six months by reviving immune cells suppressed by the tumor microenvironment. Glioblastoma carries a near-universal death sentence under standard of care, yet this cheap, off-patent vitamin is receiving minimal mainstream attention. If confirmed, the implications for a multibillion-dollar oncology drug market are obvious — and threatening.

articles.title: Ivermectin and Repurposed Drugs in Cancer: What Oncologists Won't Say But the Data Suggests
articles.summary: Dr. William Makis, a physician with extensive oncology research credentials, argues publicly that cheap, off-patent drugs like ivermectin show meaningful anticancer mechanisms that the profit-driven standard-of-care system has zero financial incentive to pursue. The medical establishment's refusal to fund or replicate this research is not an oversight — it is a business decision. Patients with terminal diagnoses are being denied options that exist in the literature.

articles.title: Antidepressants: The Harms They Don't Put in the Brochure
articles.summary: A detailed scientific review examines both the documented benefits and the frequently minimized harms of antidepressants — a drug class now prescribed to hundreds of millions globally. The piece confronts the gap between what clinical trials report and what patients actually experience, including dependency, sexual dysfunction, and emotional blunting that regulators have been slow to mandate disclosure on. The question isn't whether antidepressants help anyone — it's why the harm side of the ledger has been systematically underweighted for decades.

articles.title: Beta Bionics Hid iLet Safety Data From Investors — FDA Compliance Failures Now Trigger Fraud Lawsuit
articles.summary: Beta Bionics allegedly misled investors about the safety, efficacy, and regulatory standing of its iLet insulin delivery device, sending its stock down 37% when the truth emerged. A securities fraud class action has now been filed, with the complaint period covering July 2025 through February 2026. This is the medical device industry's playbook: overstate safety, capture regulatory goodwill, and let retail investors and patients absorb the fallout.

articles.title: Hims & Hers Faces Fraud Lawsuit After FTC Exposes What the Company Was Telling Investors vs. Reality

The case exposes how direct-to-consumer telehealth companies operating outside the traditional pharma model can replicate its worst instincts: overpromise, underdeliver, and hide the gap. Investors and patients were both misled.

articles.title: Independence Blue Cross Pays $22.5M to Settle Medicare Advantage Fraud — Diagnosis Codes Inflated, Taxpayers Looted

Medicare Advantage fraud of this type is a known, documented industry practice that saves insurers billions annually while regulators look away. This settlement is a slap on the wrist for conduct that would bankrupt a small provider.

The suppression here is not a conspiracy — it is capitalism: there is no patent, therefore there is no investment.

This is regulatory capture dressed up as science: the standard moves to meet the product, not the other way around.
